title: A Cart at the Supermarket Entrance
subtheme: A Cart at the Supermarket Entrance
description: Choose a wheeled basket before beginning the grocery aisles.
cardDescription: Choose a wheeled basket before beginning the grocery aisles.
focus: The setting is a Cart at the Supermarket Entrance. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Small wheeled vehicle used to carry a load
Round part that turns on an axle
Part held when carrying or using something
Passage between rows of seats or shelves
Material such as iron or copper

answerNotes.CART: A cart carries a load on wheels. A grocery cart's basket holds the food while its handle guides the movement.
answerNotes.WHEEL: A wheel rotates around an axle. Its tire is an outer covering, not another name for the entire wheel.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.BASKET: A basket is made by weaving flexible material. Its open structure and carrying handle make it useful for collecting garden produce.
answerNotes.AISLE: An aisle is a passage between rows. In a theater it lets people reach seats without climbing over them.
answerNotes.GROCERY: Grocery describes food and household shopping. A list records intended purchases; the bags contain what was actually bought.
answerNotes.LIST: A list records items in order. Checking off a purchased item is different from changing the price or quantity of it.
answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.
answerNotes.METAL: Metal names a family of materials including iron, copper, and aluminum. The word does not identify which metal a particular tool contains.

title: Reading Prices on the Grocery Shelf
subtheme: Reading Prices on the Grocery Shelf
description: Compare package sizes and costs before making a choice.
cardDescription: Compare package sizes and costs before making a choice.
focus: The setting is reading Prices on the Grocery Shelf. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: U.S. money unit of one hundred cents
Event at which goods are offered for money
Measurement of how big something is
One thing on a shopping list
Single measure used to compare prices
Small label attached to an item
Look at two things to see differences

answerNotes.PRICE: Price is the amount asked for an item. Change is money returned after a customer pays more than that amount.
answerNotes.LABEL: A label identifies an item or its contents. It can carry a name, date, size, or address depending on the scene.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is a horizontal storage surface. A drawer is a compartment that slides in and out.
answerNotes.DOLLAR: One U.S. dollar equals one hundred cents. Its value can be represented by one bill or several different combinations of coins.
answerNotes.SIZE: Size describes how big something is. A unit price compares cost for the same quantity, helping when package sizes differ.
answerNotes.ITEM: An item is one entry or object in a group. The same list can include individual foods, packages, and other household supplies.
answerNotes.LIST: A list records items in order. Checking off a purchased item is different from changing the price or quantity of it.

solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Flexible sack with an opening at the top
Hold and move something from place to place
Line where fabric pieces are joined
Sturdy and able to support weight

answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.CLOTH: Cloth means fabric. A cloth used for wiping is an object made from that material, not a different substance.
answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.
answerNotes.BASKET: A basket is made by weaving flexible material. Its open structure and carrying handle make it useful for collecting garden produce.
answerNotes.GROCERY: Grocery describes food and household shopping. A list records intended purchases; the bags contain what was actually bought.
answerNotes.STITCH: A stitch is one unit of worked thread or yarn. Many stitches together form a seam, knitted row, or decorative pattern.
answerNotes.SEAM: A seam joins pieces of fabric. A hem finishes an edge instead of joining two separate pieces.

title: Counting Change at the Checkout
description: Count coins returned after paying the checkout total.
cardDescription: Count coins returned after paying the checkout total.
focus: The setting is counting Change at the Checkout. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Money returned when a payment exceeds the selling amount
Common name for a U.S. one-cent coin
Money paid as bills or coins
The final sum owed for a purchase
Give money for goods or work

answerNotes.CHANGE: Change is the money returned when payment exceeds the price. The word can include several coins rather than just one.
answerNotes.COIN: A coin is a metal piece of money. The value depends on the currency and period; Bible stories do not use modern U.S. coins.
answerNotes.NICKEL: A U.S. nickel is worth five cents. The name does not mean the entire coin is made of pure nickel.
answerNotes.DIME: A U.S. dime is worth ten cents. Two nickels have the same value, although they are different coins.
answerNotes.QUARTER: A U.S. quarter is worth twenty-five cents. Four quarters make one dollar.
answerNotes.CASH: Cash means physical money such as bills and coins. A check gives an instruction to transfer money rather than being cash itself.
answerNotes.DOLLAR: One U.S. dollar equals one hundred cents. Its value can be represented by one bill or several different combinations of coins.
answerNotes.RECEIPT: A receipt records a completed payment. A bill asks for payment, so the two papers serve different purposes.

solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Take items out of bags or boxes
Container with a base and sides
Raised surface where customers are served
Food baked from flour and dough
Sweet produce such as an apple
Cupboard or small room for storing food

answerNotes.GROCERY: Grocery describes food and household shopping. A list records intended purchases; the bags contain what was actually bought.
answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.
answerNotes.BOX: A box is a container rather than its contents. In a hobby clue, a kit may come in a box but the two words are not interchangeable.
answerNotes.JAR: A jar has a wide opening that makes spooning and filling easier. A bottle usually has a narrower neck.
answerNotes.COUNTER: A counter is a raised work or serving surface. In a shop it separates the customer area from the worker's space.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is a horizontal storage surface. A drawer is a compartment that slides in and out.
answerNotes.MILK: Milk is a dairy liquid used in drinks and batters. Cream is the richer portion, with a higher fat content.
answerNotes.BREAD: Bread may be a whole loaf or pieces cut from it. A loaf is counted as a whole, while a slice is one flat portion.
answerNotes.FRUIT: Everyday fruit dishes can mix several kinds of plant produce. The serving word is culinary and does not require a botanical classification.
